evidence: Cic. Fam. 11.1.1: heri vesperī apud mē Hirtius fuit (Lewis & Short s.v. heri)
terms.comment: Of the evening before, up to bedtime; of the night itself, proximā nocte. Heri has a short final i (see yesterday evening).

evidence: Cic. Cat. 1.1: quid proximā, quid superiōre nocte ēgerīs
terms.comment: With proximā nocte beside it, “the night before”. Proxima nox is the nearest night, so in a future context it is the coming night: proximā nocte, on the following night (Traupman 88).
